title: Why bootstrapping beats VC money: unicorn collapses and the Holdco as your own VC
summary: John argues that heavily funded startups are collapsing while profitable bootstrapped companies thrive. Too much money weakens a startup, user-funded businesses stay focused on users, and the best path is bootstrap first, use VC only for growth after PMF, or run a Holdco of cash cow projects as your own VC.

principles.text: Too much funding makes you weak: you look productive but build no real strength.
principles.quote: Having too much money while building your startup is like going to a gym with fake weights. You lift them, and it all looks good, but you gain no muscles.

principles.text: Let users fund the business so your focus stays on users, not on your next round or on VCs and journalists.
principles.quote: To build great stuff for the users, the business must be funded by users. In this case your whole focus is on the users, not on your next round and VC/Journalist.

principles.text: Bootstrap first, then use VC money for growth only after product-market fit.
principles.quote: I believe the best startups will be bootstrapped and use VC money for growth after PMF.

principles.text: Bootstrapped founders have alternatives to VC: community rounds, cheap loans, and pre-sales.
principles.quote: We will see many bootstrapped founders opting for alternatives, too: community rounds, cheap loans, and pre-sales.

principles.text: Run a Holdco of simple cash cow projects and act as your own VC when needed.
principles.quote: An even better option is to run a Holdco with sole simple cash cow projects that bring in money every month and then act as your own VC when needed.

principles.text: The future of SaaS and non-deep-tech startups is efficient bootstrapped small teams or solo founders.
principles.quote: The future of SaaS and Non-Deep/Hard-Tech startups is this: highly efficient bootstrapped small teams or even solo founders and indie makers.
